case_name: Chitra Sengupta vs Dhruba Jyoti Sengupta
facts_of_case: Wife-appellant filed an application for maintenance pendente lite and cost of litigation under Section 24, Hindu Marriage Act. She also sought a temporary injunction restraining the husband from marrying again during the pendency of the appeal.

legal_principles.principle: The amount of a husband's income may not be within the knowledge of the wife, particularly in cases where the relation is strained and spouses are living apart.
legal_principles.held: In a case like this, the onus would be on the husband to disclose the same and if he fails to do so without any good reasons, the Court would be entitled to presume against him and to accept the allegations of the wife as to the amount of income derived from such reasonable sources as would be available to her.
use_in: divorce cases where income is disputed

legal_principles.principle: In affidavits on interlocutory application, statements true to one's belief can legitimately go in provided the grounds thereof are stated.
legal_principles.held: The petitioner having clearly disclosed the source of her information and the name of the informant with the latter's detailed address, her statements do not suffer from any legal infirmity.
use_in: cases where affidavits are used as evidence

outcome.final_order: The court granted maintenance pendente lite and cost of litigation to the wife-appellant.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for maintenance pendente lite
preparing an application for temporary injunction in a matrimonial dispute
advising on the implications of Section 24, Hindu Marriage Act
